relations.subject: vector-index:composite-vector-index
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (promoted predicate) - same relation direction already established in cloud/vector-index/use-vector-indexes.json
relations.evidence: If a Composite Vector index has multiple index keys, the leading index key may be a scalar field, rather than the vector field. This enables the Index Service to pre-filter using a scalar field. This is a key advantage that a Composite Vector index has over a Hyperscale Vector index with included scalar fields.

relations.subject: vector-index:composite-vector-index
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (watchlist predicate) - the 'Quantization and Centroid Settings' (#algo_settings), IVF/SQ/PQ subsections, and algorithm-settings-examples table on this page are near-verbatim identical to the same sections on hyperscale-vector-index.md
relations.evidence: Composite Vector index uses several algorithms to organize its data to improve its performance. One of these algorithms, [Inverted File (IVF)](vectors-and-indexes-overview.md#IVF), has a setting you can adjust to control how it subdivides the dataset. The other algorithms that Composite Vector index uses do not have settings you can adjust.

relations.subject: vector-index:approx-vector-distance
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (promoted predicate) - production-query context; contrasts with the opposite-direction relation logged in vector-index-best-practices.json (VECTOR_DISTANCE preferred only for recall-rate ground-truth measurement)
relations.evidence: To use your Composite Vector index, use the `SELECT` statement with an `ORDER BY` clause containing a call to the `APPROX_VECTOR_DISTANCE` function. This function selects the Composite Vector index when you query the vector key that the index covers... You can also perform vector comparisons using the VECTOR\_DISTANCE function. This function does not select a Hyperscale Vector index or a Composite Vector Index, but performs a brute-force comparison.
